newsitem.title: CHINA: China punishes 12 banks, brokerages in share case.
newsitem.headline: China punishes 12 banks, brokerages in share case.

text.p: The China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC) has punished and fined 12 bank branches and brokerages for illegally bidding for shares on credit, the China Securities newspaper reported Saturday.

Analysts said this was the largest number of financial institutions publicly punished at the same time for such an offence and showed Beijing's resolve to crack down on irregularities in the securities markets.

The CSRC imposed a fine of 1.13 million yuan ($136,000) on the Jiangmen branch of the Guangdong Development Bank for using 568.94 million yuan ($68.5 million) on Aug. 30 to bid for shares of Qinghai Mingjiao, which listed local currency shares on the Shenzhen stock market, the newspaper said.

It imposed a fine of 790,000 yuan ($95,180) on the Zhongshan Securities Co. for bidding 398.12 million yuan ($48.0 million) on Aug. 27 for shares of Jiangsu Supu, which listed local currency shares on the Shanghai stock market, it said.
It also imposed a fine of 690,000 yuan ($83,136) on Hainan Gangao International Trust and Investment for bidding 343.5 million yuan ($41.4 million) on Aug. 30 for shares of Qinghai Mingjiao.
Chinese securities regulations strictly ban any kind of stock trading on credit.

Such practices made huge volumes of credit flow illegally into the stock market, made the subscription rates for new shares fall to astonishingly low levels and deprived small and medium-size investors of the chance to buy new shares, the newspaper said in an angry front-page editorial.
In China, prices of nearly all new issues rise sharply after listing, largely because of speculation, making them very popular with investors.

The editorial warned that those responsible for illegalities would be stripped of their official titles and their illegal earnings would be confiscated. "Such harsh punishments should be a lesson for others," it said.

The CRSC listed seven other banks, brokerages and financial institutions which it said had illegally bid for shares in Qinghai Mingjiao and two others which it said had illegally bid for shares in Jiangsu Supu.

Such actions contravened China's securities regulations, seriously interfered with the normal order of the securities market and destroyed the principles of fairness and equality in the market, the CSRC said.

On Friday, the official media said branches of the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China and the China International Trust and Investment Corp. had been disciplined for illegally lending money to securities firms.
A stock analyst with a major Chinese securities house said the incident was part of the campaign by the authorities to clearly separate the activities of banks and securities houses.

"The action comes after the surge in domestic stocks this year with Beijing's blessing," said a second analyst. "The authorities are afraid that the market, with official support, will go out of control with speculative activity growing."
